text:
maria-peopleops: Hey team — quick help please. My partner had to go to the ER while we were visiting family out of state (Portland) over the weekend. We got an EOB and the carrier shows 0 paid with reason 'out of network'. Our PCP and usual specialists are in CA and show as in-network. Does the Redwood plan cover emergency care out-of-network? And what's the fastest way to appeal/submit the hospital bill so we don't get stuck?

ben-hr: In emergencies the plan generally treats ER visits as in-network, yes. You should be able to file an appeal with the carrier and submit the hospital's itemized bill + the EOB. If you want, we can open a case on your behalf to help escalate.

maria-peopleops: Thanks — can you confirm what to upload and where? The carrier portal was kinda confusing. Also worried about the billing code they used (they listed CPT 99285) — does that matter?

benefits-bot: Hi! Filing checklist for out-of-network emergency claims: 1) Attach carrier EOB, 2) Attach itemized hospital bill (PDF), 3) Add ER discharge summary or physician note showing emergency medical condition, 4) Provider name + NPI, 5) Member ID and dates of service. Deadline: carrier requires appeals within 90 days of EOB date. Portal: https://benefits.redwood.com/claims -> "Submit appeal". If you prefer email, send to benefits@redwood.com with subject: "Appeal: OON ER claim — MEMBER_NAME — DOS 2026-02-14".

samir: Also save any receipts or transport (ambulance) bills. The CPT code might affect pricing but shouldn't invalidate an emergency claim. The discharge summary is usually the most important doc to prove emergency status.

ben-hr: If you want me to open the case I can. Helpful if you paste the claim number from the EOB and attach the PDFs. Example email body you can copy:

```
Subject: Appeal: OON ER claim — Maria Partner — DOS 2026-02-14

Hello benefits team,
Please open an appeal for the attached out-of-network emergency claim. Member ID: XXXXXX. Carrier claim#: 987654321. Attached: EOB, itemized bill, discharge summary. Please confirm receipt and next steps.

Thanks,
Maria
```

maria-peopleops: Copying that — appreciate it. I'll upload the docs now and DM you the claim number. Really appreciate the quick help :heart:

ben-hr: No problem. Ping me once uploaded and I'll follow-up with the carrier. If they request pre-auth retroactively (rare for ER), we'll advise next steps.

samir: FYI — if carrier denies after appeal, we can request an external review through state regulator. Keep receipts and any clinical notes.
